definitions.explanation: A traditional Japanese freestanding panel or series of connected panels that can be folded, used for decoration or to divide spaces.

examples.japanese: {床|とこ}の{間|ま}に{金|きん}{屏風|びょうぶ}を{飾|かざ}った。
examples.english: We displayed a gold folding screen in the alcove.

examples.japanese: {雛人形|ひなにんぎょう}の{後|うし}ろに{屏風|びょうぶ}を{立|た}てる。
examples.english: We put a folding screen behind the Hina dolls.

examples.japanese: {国宝|こくほう}の{屏風絵|びょうぶえ}を{美術館|びじゅつかん}で{見|み}た。
examples.english: I saw a national treasure folding screen painting at the museum.

notes:
STRUCTURE: Traditional {屏風|びょうぶ} consists of multiple panels ({曲|きょく}) connected by hinges:
・{二曲|にきょく} - 2 panels
・{四曲|よんきょく} - 4 panels
・{六曲|ろっきょく} - 6 panels (most common)
・{八曲|はっきょく} - 8 panels

TYPES:
・{金屏風|きんびょうぶ} - gold folding screen (used at weddings, ceremonies)
・{銀屏風|ぎんびょうぶ} - silver folding screen
・{屏風絵|びょうぶえ} - painted folding screen
・{風炉先屏風|ふろさきびょうぶ} - tea ceremony screen

CULTURAL SIGNIFICANCE:
・Famous historical {屏風絵|びょうぶえ} include works by artists like {俵屋宗達|たわらやそうたつ} and {尾形光琳|おがたこうりん}
・Used in formal ceremonies, tea rooms, and traditional Japanese interiors
・{雛|ひな}{祭|まつ}り displays often include a miniature gold screen

ETYMOLOGY: From Chinese 屏風 (píngfēng), meaning "wind screen" - originally used to block drafts.
